title: Tunisian Egg Brik with Potato, Capers and Harissa
summary: Crisp fried pastry parcels hide a soft potato filling with a whole egg inside, finished with a sharp hit of capers and parsley.

ingredients.item: large floury potato (about 280 g), peeled and diced
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Mash
steps.text: Boil the diced potato in salted water until tender, drain and mash with 1 tbsp olive oil.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the frying oil in a deep pan to 175°C.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Lay a wrapper on a saucer, spoon 3 tbsp mashed potato into the centre and press a hollow in it, then dab with harissa if using and scatter over the capers and parsley.

steps.title: Crack
steps.text: Crack an egg into the hollow, fold one corner of the wrapper over to the opposite corner to enclose the filling and egg in a triangle, and press the edges to seal.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Slide the parcel into the oil away from you and fry for about 1 minute until golden underneath, then flip and fry for about 1 minute more, longer if a set yolk is wanted.

steps.title: Repeat
steps.text: Lift out, drain briefly, then make the remaining parcels one at a time.

tips: Work quickly once the egg is in the wrapper so it doesn't leak before folding.
Fry one parcel at a time to keep control of the folding and the frying.
For vulnerable guests, fry a little longer so the yolk is fully set rather than runny.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best eaten straight from the pan while hot and crisp; not suitable for keeping or reheating. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
